name: Cuts locked to the music

source.description: Measured in three inspected references: visual cuts fall on musical beats or audio hits far more often than chance.

technique: Scene cuts and word changes land on the soundtrack's beats or hits, so picture and sound feel like one gesture and the edit's rhythm is felt rather than noticed.
purpose: Rhythm and impact; makes fast cutting comfortable.
visual_behaviour: Each cut coincides with a drum hit or note onset; holds last whole numbers of beats.
mechanics: Beat grid from the track's tempo and phase; cue times snapped to the grid (or to detected onsets) within about one frame.

decomposition.timing: Measured: Measured at analyzer 1.2: ref-92c22222a2 60% of boundaries within 60 ms of the estimated 129 bpm grid (chance 26%), 80% within 50 ms of an onset (chance 41%); ref-392ee4d0f9 80% near an onset (chance 31%); ref-736d4ef2c2 40% near the 129 bpm grid (chance 26%, weak).

parameters.name: bpm
parameters.description: Track tempo (measure it; the corpus tool estimates it)

failure_modes: Snapping cuts that need reading time onto a fast grid
Using an estimated tempo without checking the phase by ear

implementation.approach: Studio.rhythm.grid(bpm, {offset}) and Studio.rhythm.snap for cue times; Studio.comp.wordBeats accepts a tempo grid. scripts/reference-corpus.py measures onset and beat alignment of a finished or reference cut.

additional_tooling.justification: Tempo and onset estimates come from the corpus tool's numpy analysis; Earshot or real-sfx on the render host can refine them.

limitations: Tempo estimates are autocorrelation-based and can lock to half or double tempo

provenance.observed: Cuts in the word section align with the estimated beat grid (measured 0.60 vs 0.26 chance): 11.25, 11.72, 12.18 and 12.65 s are within 60 ms of the 129 bpm grid; 11.48 s sits on an onset but off the grid. Checked 2026-11-28 from automated.audio.

Boundaries coincide with audio onsets: 4 of 5 within 67 ms of an onset (2.10, 3.77, 8.47, 13.17 s; chance 0.31); the 5.57 s cut is 123 ms off. Only 2 of 5 sit on the 64.6 bpm grid (2.10, 13.17 s; chance 0.13). Recomputed 2026-11-28 from automated.audio.

Boundaries sit near the estimated 129 bpm grid more often than chance, weakly: 4 of 10 within 60 ms (3.82, 13.10, 16.88, 21.57 s; chance 0.26). Of the four hard cuts only 16.88 and 21.57 s are on the grid. Recomputed 2026-11-28 from automated.audio.

6 of 8 boundaries lie within 50 ms of an onset (0.25, 3.35, 9.38, 10.69, 11.97, 12.43 s; chance 42%); tempo estimate 129 bpm, medium confidence. Recomputed 2026-11-28 from automated.audio (13.13 s, cited before, is off any onset).
75% of 8 boundaries within 50 ms of an onset (chance 46%) and 75% near the 129 bpm beat (chance 26%).

In a lyric video 6 of 12 boundaries carry an accent within 100 ms (9.20, 10.35, 11.47, 13.80, 18.32, 22.88 s; 0.50 against chance 0.14): picture changes land on the song's onsets because each cut is a new phrase.
Section glitch cuts on whole seconds of a 120 bpm grid (near the beat 0.40 against chance 0.24; accent within 100 ms 0.40 against 0.16).

Six hard cuts exactly on whole seconds (86% within 67 ms of an onset, chance 0.35) but none carries a strong accent (0 of 7, chance 0.12): the cut sits on the downbeat and the hit comes on the next line.
20 of 28 cuts land within 67 ms of an onset (chance 0.46), but only 4 near the estimated beat (chance 0.19) and 5 on a strong accent (chance 0.17): cuts follow onsets in busy music.
5 of 6 boundaries within 50 ms of an onset (chance 0.27); the one hard cut (5.65 s) and the foreground pass (4.30 s) also carry the strongest accents (2 of 6, chance 0.12).

A climax montage of 11 style cards at 0.10-0.27 s each (median 0.13 s, 11.27-13.03 s); accents 0.23-0.24 s apart (11.54, 11.77, 12.00, 12.24 s) each within 0-40 ms of a cut (11.50, 11.77, 11.97, 12.20 s).

evidence.notes: wordBeats times from a 120 bpm grid are exact.

licensing_notes: Technique only; measured from user-supplied references. No audio is reused.
